text:
incident-bot: PAGER: gpu-queue-growth alert for cluster-prod-eu-west. autoscaler reported max_nodes_reached for gpu-nodepool (limit=48). queue length trending up rapidly. escalation: oncall.

sara (oncall): Ack. seeing a big backlog in the inference queue, lots of 429s from the routing layer. I’m attaching current queue sizes and node counts.

jing (sre): Copy. Can you dump autoscaler status and pod pending reasons? also paste the replica count for model-serving-deployment-prod.

sara (oncall): quick stats: queue depth ~ 14k requests, average wait ~ 22s, token throughput down 30%. GPU nodepool at 48/48. K8s shows ~12 pods pending with reason "Insufficient allocatable gpu".

omar (infra): autoscaler logs show attempts to create nodes but cloud quota refused: "Node quota exceeded for project". cloud console shows per-region GPU quota is at maximum.

kyle (platform-eng): Oof. We hit the hard node quota, looks like autoscaler can't breach the account limit. Any short-term mitigation: reduce per-pod GPU requests (if safe), spin up a cpu-only fallback, or temporarily shift lower-priority workloads to another pool.

sara (oncall): Immediate steps I'm doing: 1) enable request-level throttling to shed non-critical batches, 2) flip routing policy to fall back to a cached-model variant for heavy customers, 3) create incident ticket for quota increase request to cloud.

leila (cust-succ): Heads up — Customer X (finance-prod) is seeing elevated latencies, reported a few failed jobs. I'm drafting a short notification with ETA.

jing (sre): Commands I'm running now to get details:
```
# check pending pods
kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep Pending
# autoscaler status
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler | tail -n 200
# check nodepool size
gcloud container node-pools describe gpu-pool --cluster prod-eu-west --format json
```

sara (oncall): I pushed a temporary rate-limit at the ingress rule: `/v1/generate` 80% of baseline for non-paying tenants. Should reduce new load within ~30s. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

omar (infra): Quota request submitted to cloud support with priority P1. Request ID: CS-794512. They responded with "under review", ETA unclear. Meanwhile, I can spin up a temporary non-gpu fallback nodepool (cpu-only) and redirect low-cost models to it. That will reduce GPU pressure without changing model behavior for critical tenants.

kyle (platform-eng): For the fallback, we need a lightweight runtime image and config. I'll push a canary config to route model-small and model-medium to cpu-pool. Deploy command:
```
kubectl apply -f k8s/overrides/fallback-route-cpu.yaml -n prod
```
Do we have capacity in cpu pools?

omar (infra): Yes, cpu pool has spare nodes. I'm starting the nodepool create now: `gcloud container node-pools create cpu-fallback --cluster prod-eu-west --num-nodes=6 --machine-type=n1-standard-8`

incident-bot: Status update: queue depth decreased 12% since throttling applied. autoscaler still at max_nodes_reached.

sara (oncall): I'm seeing pending pods slowly getting scheduled as cpu-fallback becomes ready. Good sign. Customer X still has some failures; working with leila on the message.

leila (cust-succ): Sent message to Customer X: "We're experiencing degraded inference throughput due to capacity constraints. We've temporarily routed lower-priority workloads to fallback infrastructure; our engineers are working on quota increase and expect improvements within the hour. We'll update you if your job is impacted further." They acknowledged, asked for an incident contact.

jing (sre): Action item: create follow-up to adjust autoscaler policy to prefer scaling GPU pool earlier (lower utilization threshold) and to allow burst nodes for short windows. Also we need cluster-level guardrails to fail open to cpu fallback instead of queue growth.

sara (oncall): Noting mitigation timeline: 00:00 apply rate-limit, 00:04 cpu-fallback nodepool creation started, 00:12 routing flip for low-priority models, 00:28 queue depth down 60% from peak.

kyle (platform-eng): For longer term: propose a change in the autoscaler config:
- reduce target utilization from 70% -> 50% for gpu pool when queue rate > 2000 req/min
- add a temporary burst policy that can exceed nodepool quota if approved by oncall (this will need billing/finance sign-off)
- implement automatic degrade-to-cpu policy with tested correctness guards

omar (infra): Cloud support responded: they can raise GPU quota but require ordering confirmation and will take ~3-4 hours for availability. Request still P1. I'll follow up and escalate with account manager.

incident-bot: Pager cleared: primary alert resolved (queue rate dropping, most pending pods scheduled on fallback). Secondary alert: follow-up ticket created for autoscaler policy and quota increase.

sara (oncall): Handoff note for next oncall (jing): workload reduced but still some residual customer impact for heavy batch jobs. Please monitor queue and cloud quota updates. If quota increases, revert fallback routing and drain cpu-fallback pool.

jing (sre): Acknowledged handoff. Will keep watch and file the post-incident doc with timeline + follow-ups: quota request tracking, autoscaler policy PR, route-degrade test coverage.

leila (cust-succ): I'll follow up with the customers we flagged and close the support tickets once we confirm stable throughput.

sara (oncall): Final notes: root cause = cloud GPU quota hit + autoscaler conservative thresholds + lack of an automatic cpu-fallback. Impact = increased latencies and some failed batch jobs for a subset of customers for ~45 minutes. Next steps: 1) follow up on quota CS-794512, 2) PR autoscaler tuning (kyle/jing), 3) add runbook step to spin cpu-fallback and communicate to customers (leila).

kyle (platform-eng): I'll open the autoscaler PR and link it here.

incident-bot: Incident thread closed for now. Reminders: attach logs and `kubectl get events` output to the postmortem, include the quota request ID and timeline. :white_check_mark:
